         2                  ACTING PRESIDENT STEWART-COUSINS:

         3       The Senate will please come to order.

         4                  I ask everyone present to rise and

         5       recite with me the Pledge of Allegiance to our

         6       Flag.

         7                  (Whereupon, the assemblage recited

         8       the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag.)

         9                  ACTING PRESIDENT STEWART-COUSINS:

        10       In the absence of clergy, may we all bow our

        11       heads for a moment of silence.

        12                  (Whereupon, the assemblage

        13       respected a moment of silence.)

        14                  ACTING PRESIDENT STEWART-COUSINS:

        15       Thank you.

        16                  Senator Smith.

        17                  SENATOR SMITH:    Yes, Madam

        18       President.  Is there a proclamation from the

        19       Governor at the desk?

        20                  ACTING PRESIDENT STEWART-COUSINS:

        21       Yes, Senator Smith, there is a proclamation

        22       here at the desk.

        23                  The Secretary will read.

        24                  THE SECRETARY:    "Pursuant to the

         1       power vested in me by Article IV, Section 3 of

         2       the Constitution, I hereby convene the Senate

         3       of the State of New York in Extraordinary

         4       Session, at the Capitol, in the City of

         5       Albany, on the sixth day of July, two thousand

         6       nine, at three o'clock p.m., for the purpose

         7       of considering legislation I will submit with

         8       respect to various subjects, and considering

         9       gubernatorial nominations.

        10                  "Given under my hand and the Privy

        11       Seal of the State in the City of Albany this

        12       first day of July in the year two thousand

        13       nine, by the Governor, David A. Paterson."

        14                  ACTING PRESIDENT STEWART-COUSINS:

        15       The proclamation having been read, the Senate

        16       is in extraordinary session.

        17                  Senator Smith.

        18                  SENATOR SMITH:    Yes, Madam

        19       President, would you please recognize my

        20       colleague Senator Dean Skelos.

        21                  ACTING PRESIDENT STEWART-COUSINS:

        22       Senator Skelos.

        23                  SENATOR SKELOS:    Thank you.

        24                  Good afternoon, Senator

         1       Stewart-Cousins.

         3       Good afternoon.

         4                  SENATOR SKELOS:    At the

         5       Governor's request, and in keeping with the

         6       decision of the court, we convene this

         7       extraordinary session.

         8                  As I've stated before, the

         9       designation of a presiding officer should be

        10       made by Senator Espada or myself pursuant to

        11       the votes which took place on June 8th.

        12       Accordingly, we do not recognize that you are

        13       the appropriately designated presiding

        14       officer.

        15                  Therefore, I'd request that the

        16       agenda be laid aside and move that the Senate

        17       adjourn this special session sine die.

        18                  ACTING PRESIDENT STEWART-COUSINS:

        19       Thank you, Senator Skelos.

        20                  Senator Smith.

        21                  SENATOR SMITH:    Yes, thank you,

        22       Madam President.  So good to see you this

        23       afternoon.

        24                  Before we move on this day, I would

         5       moved on, some will be moving on, some are

         6       still here at the Senate.

         7                  They have had obviously an

         8       extraordinary experience this year.  It is one

         9       that provides them with the ability to learn

        10       not only what state government is about, but

        11       also to see how the inner workings of one of

        12       the most distinguished bodies in this country

        13       performs.

        15       those who are here and who they've worked for.

        16       We had Matthew Gass, who worked in our press

        17       office.  We had Sara Bangs, who worked in

        18       Majority Counsel.  We had Linda Cohen, who

        19       worked for Senator Bill Perkins.

        23       Marcellino.  We had Dilay Watson, who worked

        24       for Senator Sampson.  Martin McGuinness, who I
